# A local build that names a run in GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN locks each org module head
# the first go command of the run resolves. Every later go command of the same
# run builds that version instead of resolving its own head, which is what makes
# a build of many go commands pay for each ls-remote once. A new run resolves
# the head again, so a commit that lands between runs is picked up.
#
# This needs no CI: the run name alone selects the lock. The store is named too,
# here as a directory, so the test leaves nothing in the user cache.

[!git] skip

# Every org repository is a local file:// clone behind an insteadOf rule.
env TESTGOVCSREMOTE=

env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher${/}.gitconfig
env HOME=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher
env GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file
env GOPRIVATE=github.com/wow-look-at-my
[!GOOS:windows] exec git config --global 'url.file://'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'
[GOOS:windows]  exec git config --global 'url.file:///'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'

env GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Go Gopher'
env GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='gopher@golang.org'
env GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME
env GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL

# No CI: the run name, not GITHUB_ACTIONS, is what locks the heads.
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=
env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=
env GITHUB_RUN_ID=
env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN=wow-look-at-my/consumer/4242/1
[!GOOS:windows] env LOCKS=file://$WORK/locks
[GOOS:windows]  env LOCKS=file:///$WORK/locks
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$LOCKS

cd $WORK/alpha
exec git init
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'alpha main'
exec git branch -m main

# The first go command of the run resolves the head and locks it.
cd $WORK/m
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main$'
exists $WORK/locks

# alpha moves while the run is under way.
cd $WORK/alpha
cp $WORK${/}alpha-next${/}alpha.go alpha.go
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
exec git commit -am 'alpha next'

# Another go command of the same run builds the locked version, not the new head.
cd $WORK/m2
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main$'

# A new run resolves the head again and picks up the move.
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN=wow-look-at-my/consumer/9999/1
cd $WORK/m3
go run .
stdout '^alpha-next$'

-- $WORK/home/gopher/.gitconfig --
[user]
	name = Go Gopher
	email = gopher@golang.org
-- $WORK/alpha/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha

go 1.21
-- $WORK/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-main" }
-- $WORK/alpha-next/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-next" }
-- $WORK/m/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/m/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/m2/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/m2/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/m3/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/m3/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
